tools.name: Add a repository collaborator
tools.description: Adds a GitHub user as a repository collaborator, or updates their permission if already a collaborator; `permission` applies to organization-owned repositories (personal ones default to 'push' and ignore this field), and an invitation may be created or permissions updated directly.

input.title: AddARepositoryCollaboratorRequest

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case sensitive.
repo.human_parameter_description: Provide the short name of the repository where you want to add the collaborator (without .git). This tells us which project to update.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case sensitive.
owner.human_parameter_description: Enter the GitHub user or organization that owns the repository. This ensures the collaborator is added to the correct account.

username.title: Username
username.description: The GitHub handle for the user account to add as a collaborator. Cannot be the same as the repository owner, as owners are automatically collaborators.
username.human_parameter_description: Enter the GitHub username of the person you want to add. This is the account that will receive access to the repository. Note: You cannot add the repository owner as a collaborator since they already have full access.

permission.title: Permission
permission.description: Permission level for the collaborator. For organization-owned repositories, valid values are `pull` (read-only), `triage` (manage issues/PRs), `push` (read/write), `maintain` (manage most settings), `admin` (full control), or a custom repository role name if defined by the owning organization. This parameter is ignored for personal repositories, which grant `push` access.
permission.human_parameter_description: Choose the level of access to grant this collaborator (read, triage, write, maintain, admin, or a custom role). Pick the lowest level they need; personal repositories will default to write access.

input.description: Request schema for adding a collaborator to a GitHub repository.

tools.name: Commit Multiple Files
tools.description: Tool to atomically create, update, or delete multiple files in a GitHub repository as a single commit. Uses Git Data APIs to avoid SHA mismatch conflicts that occur with the Contents API when multiple files are modified in parallel. Use when you need to make multi-file changes reliably. BRANCH CREATION: When committing to a new branch (e.g., 'fix/my-fix' or 'feature/new-feature'), you MUST provide 'base_branch' (typically 'main' or 'master') to create the branch from. If the branch already exists, base_branch is not needed. This action handles race conditions automatically: if the branch is updated by another commit between fetching the HEAD and updating the reference (resulting in a 422 'not a fast forward' error), the action will retry by refetching the HEAD and rebasing changes. Use max_retries to control this behavior.

repo.description: Repository name (without .git extension)

email.description: Email address of the author or committer

tools.name: Compare two commits
tools.description: Compares two commit points (commits, branches, tags, or SHAs) within a repository or across forks, using `BASE...HEAD` or `OWNER:REF...OWNER:REF` format for the `basehead` parameter.

input.title: CompareTwoCommitsRequest

page.title: Page
page.description: Page number of the results to fetch, for pagination when the number of differences (commits or files) is large.
page.human_parameter_description: Which page of results to view when there are many commits or files. Start at 1 and increase to see more pages.

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.
repo.human_parameter_description: The name of the repository where you want to compare commits. Use the repo name as it appears on GitHub (without .git).

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: The username or organization name that owns the repository. This field is not case-sensitive.
owner.human_parameter_description: The GitHub account that owns the repository you want to compare in. Enter the username or organization name so we can find the right repo.

basehead.title: Basehead
basehead.description: A string specifying the base and head references to compare, in the format `BASE...HEAD`. `BASE` and `HEAD` can be branch names (e.g., `main...develop`), tag names (e.g., `v1.0.0...v1.1.0`), or commit SHAs (abbreviated or full 40-character format). Both abbreviated and full SHAs are accepted; full 40-character SHAs are recommended for reliability in large repositories. Both references must exist in the specified repository. To compare branches across forks in the same network, use the format `OWNER:REF...OWNER:REF` (e.g., `octocat:main...another-user:main`). Do NOT pass GitHub URLs - only plain reference strings like 'main...develop' are accepted.
basehead.human_parameter_description: The two points you want to compare, written as BASE...HEAD (for example, main...develop). Use branch names, tags, or commit SHAs in any length - both abbreviated and full 40-character SHAs work.

per_page.title: Per Page
per_page.description: Number of results (e.g., files or commits) to return per page, with a maximum of 100, for pagination.
per_page.human_parameter_description: How many items to show per page in the results. Choose a larger number to see more at once (up to 100).

input.description: Request schema for `CompareTwoCommits` action. Specifies the repository and the two commit points (base and head) to compare.

base.human_parameter_description: The branch you want to merge your changes into, usually 'main' or 'develop'. Choose a branch that already exists in the target repository.

body.title: Body

tools.name: Search issues and pull requests
tools.description: Searches GitHub issues and pull requests using a flexible query with qualifiers, sorting, and pagination. Use this action when you need to find issues or pull requests across repositories using search criteria like author, labels, state, milestone, or date ranges. This action searches across all repositories accessible to the authenticated user unless constrained by qualifiers like repo:, user:, or org:.

input.title: SearchIssuesRequest

q.title: Q
q.description: Search query string for issues and pull requests. Supports qualifiers: `repo:owner/repo`, `user:username`, `org:orgname`, `author:username`, `assignee:username`, `mentions:username`, `commenter:username`, `involves:username`, `label:labelname`, `milestone:title`, `state:open|closed`, `type:pr|issue`, `is:pr|issue|open|closed|merged|unmerged|locked|unlocked|draft`, `in:title|body|comments`, `created:YYYY-MM-DD`, `updated:YYYY-MM-DD`, `closed:YYYY-MM-DD`, `merged:YYYY-MM-DD`, `no:label|milestone|assignee`, `language:language`, `comments:n`, `reactions:n`, `interactions:n`, `project:number`, `archived:true|false`, `reviewed-by:username`. Use comparison operators (>, <, >=, <=, ..) with numeric/date qualifiers. Multiple terms use implicit AND; quote exact phrases. Example: 'repo:owner/repo is:issue state:open label:bug'

sort.title: SortEnum

tools.name: Update a reference
tools.description: Updates an existing Git reference (e.g., a branch or tag) to point to a specific commit SHA. By default, only allows fast-forward updates (where the new commit is a descendant of the current one). Set `force=true` to allow non-fast-forward updates that rewrite history. IMPORTANT: The reference must already exist - use 'Create a reference' action to create new refs.

input.title: UpdateAReferenceRequest

ref.title: Ref
ref.description: The name of the Git reference to update WITHOUT the 'refs/' prefix. For branches: use 'heads/<branch-name>' (e.g., 'heads/main', 'heads/feature-branch'). For tags: use 'tags/<tag-name>' (e.g., 'tags/v1.0.0'). Note: Branch references require 'heads/' (plural), not 'head/' (singular). Bare branch names will be automatically prefixed with 'heads/'. The reference must already exist - this endpoint only updates existing refs.
ref.human_parameter_description: The branch or tag path you want to update (without 'refs/' prefix). Use 'heads/branch-name' for branches or 'tags/tag-name' for tags. The reference must already exist.

sha.title: Sha
sha.description: The SHA1 commit hash to point this reference to. Must be exactly 40 hexadecimal characters (0-9, a-f) representing a valid commit that exists in the repository.
sha.human_parameter_description: The full 40-character commit hash you want the reference to point to. Find this by viewing commits in your repository - it's the long hexadecimal string identifying each commit.

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: Repository name, excluding `.git` extension (case-insensitive).
repo.human_parameter_description: The name of the repository where you want to update the reference. Use the exact name from the GitHub URL (without .git).

force.title: Force
force.description: Controls whether to allow non-fast-forward updates. When `false` (default), the new commit must be a direct descendant of the current commit (fast-forward only) - this prevents accidental history rewriting. When `true`, allows moving the reference to any commit, even if it means rewriting history or moving backward. Set to `true` only when you need to force-push changes, reset a branch, or intentionally rewrite commit history.
force.human_parameter_description: Set to true only if you need to rewrite history or move the branch backward. Leave false (default) for normal forward updates where the new commit builds upon the current one.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: Account owner of the repository (case-insensitive).
owner.human_parameter_description: The GitHub username or organization that owns the repository you want to change. Use the owner shown in the repository URL.

input.description: Request schema for `UpdateAReference`

tools.name: Update an issue

body.title: Body
examples:
Steps to reproduce:
1. Do this
2. Do that
Observed behavior...
body.description: New issue body; send `null` to clear, omit to leave unchanged.
body.human_parameter_description: The updated description or notes for the issue. Leave empty if you don’t want to change it.

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: Repository name, without the `.git` extension (case-insensitive).
repo.human_parameter_description: The repository where the issue lives. Enter the short repository name (not a URL).

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: Owner of the repository (case-insensitive).
owner.human_parameter_description: The account or organization that owns the repository containing the issue. Use the GitHub username or org name.

state.title: StateEnm
state.description: New issue state; omit to leave unchanged.
state.human_parameter_description: Set whether the issue should be open or closed. Leave empty to keep the current state.

title.title: Title
title.description: New issue title; send `null` to clear, omit to leave unchanged.
title.human_parameter_description: The new title you want for the issue. Leave empty if you don’t want to change it.

labels.title: Labels
labels.description: Replaces all existing labels. Send `[]` to remove all; omit to leave unchanged. Requires push access for changes.
labels.human_parameter_description: List all labels that should be on the issue; this replaces any existing labels. Leave empty if you don’t want to change them.

assignee.title: Assignee
assignee.description: DEPRECATED: Username to assign; use `assignees`. Send `null` to unassign, omit to leave unchanged.
assignee.human_parameter_description: Assign the issue to a single user by username. For modern use, prefer the 'Assignees' field to set multiple assignees.

assignees.title: Assignees
assignees.description: Replaces all existing assignees. Send `[]` to remove all; omit to leave unchanged. Requires push access for changes.
assignees.human_parameter_description: List the usernames to assign to this issue; this replaces any existing assignees. Leave empty if you don’t want to change them.

milestone.title: Milestone

milestone.human_parameter_description: Choose the milestone this issue should be associated with, using its number or title. Leave empty if you don’t want to change it.

issue_number.title: Issue Number
issue_number.human_parameter_description: The number of the issue you want to update. You can find it at the top of the issue page on GitHub.

state_reason.title: StateReasonEnm
state_reason.description: Reason for state change, considered only if `state` also changes. Valid reasons depend on the new `state`.
state_reason.human_parameter_description: Explain why the state changed (for example, completed, not planned, or reopened). Only used when you also change the state.
